title: Cheerio
author: Gopal Lahiri
stanzas: I have a wooden door in my room
in the shape of a halo, an open key.
In the night, the silence is tuned to a different
mode, it feels strange echo by echo.
Like the hush after a local train passes by
I open the door and there is nothing left
to see except the darkness; the silence
then touches me, once, twice, thrice perhaps,
the half-moon enters now through the door
shine all along with waxing and waning.
Only a rhythm remains, a movement, a turn,
you are sailing off into the distance,
I unwind like a fly catcher and glide in the open
to clasp air, to wave cheerio.
text:
I have a wooden door in my room
in the shape of a halo, an open key.

In the night, the silence is tuned to a different
mode, it feels strange echo by echo.

Like the hush after a local train passes by
I open the door and there is nothing left

to see except the darkness; the silence
then touches me, once, twice, thrice perhaps,

the half-moon enters now through the door
shine all along with waxing and waning.

Only a rhythm remains, a movement, a turn,
you are sailing off into the distance,

I unwind like a fly catcher and glide in the open
to clasp air, to wave cheerio.
